messages:
incident_bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GPU OOM spike on runtime-decode-21 (us-west-2). 4 nodes reported CUDA OOM within 3m, ~12% request error rate on /v1/generate-stream. Severity: P1. Paging oncall.
Bob (oncall): Acked. I'm looking at node pool now. hitting OOMs during streaming decode with unusual token counts.
Maya (SRE): On it. Can you paste the most recent container logs from runtime-decode-21-7bf4?
Bob (oncall): tail from node:
```
2026-03-15T03:11:02Z runtime: decode loop start session_id=abc123 max_tokens=5000
2026-03-15T03:11:02Z runtime: streaming chunk flush
2026-03-15T03:11:06Z cuda: allocation failed: out of memory
2026-03-15T03:11:06Z runtime: aborting request session_id=abc123 reason=OOM
```
Eli (Runtime): That `max_tokens=5000` is suspicious; our model-variant has lower KV cache capacity after quantization. We expect 1024 typical. Are clients sending large `max_tokens`? Could be a runaway generation loop (no stop tokens).
Jane (Customer Ops): Any immediate customer impact? I can start outreach if this affects enterprise customers.
Bob (oncall): Quick correl: traffic spike from a single API key, multiple streaming sessions with no early stops. Logs show `stop` empty and `max_tokens` high.
Maya (SRE): Mitigation plan in order:
1) Throttle streaming endpoint at edge for that API key (apply rate-limit + concurrent session cap)
2) Push runtime hotfix to enforce server-side `max_tokens` upper bound (reject or clamp >2048)
3) Disable streaming for the affected model-variant and route to non-streaming fallback smaller model
4) Recycle the 4 flapping nodes after draining
I'll run 1 & 3 now.
Eli (Runtime): Agreed. Also add temporary circuit-breaker to drop requests >2k tokens rather than attempting allocation.
Bob (oncall): Applied rate-limit on API key `acct_7X...` -> `x-ratelimit: 5/min` and concurrent_streams=2. Confirmed immediate reduction in OOM errors.
incident_bot: Incident update: error rate on /v1/generate-stream dropped from 12% -> 2% after edge throttling.
Eli (Runtime): Pushing config to router to clamp `max_tokens` server-side (hot patch):
```
# router config snippet
routes:
  - path: /v1/generate-stream
    enforce_server_max_tokens: 2048
    on_violation: clamp  # options: clamp | reject
```
Eli (Runtime): Rolling this patch to us-west-2 now. Command:
`kubectl apply -f router-clamp-usw2.yaml && kubectl rollout restart deployment/router-usw2`
Bob (oncall): Patch applied, restart done. No new OOMs in the last 3m. But two nodes still show elevated memory fragmentation—I'll cordon and drain for restart.
Maya (SRE): Doing node drain: `kubectl drain runtime-decode-21-7bf4 --ignore-daemonsets && kubectl delete pod runtime-decode-21-7bf4`
Bob (oncall): Nodes restarted and rejoined by 03:28Z. Error rate stabilized ~0.5% (background noise).
Jane (Customer Ops): Customer impact tally: we saw ~23 customer requests dropped (5 retries), 3 enterprise customers experienced transient errors (IDs: C-112, C-117, C-204). Posting to status page and starting targeted emails.
Omar (Product): Important to know root cause: was this client misconfig (malicious) or product misvalidation? Need to decide whether to block the API key or change default safety limits.
Eli (Runtime): Preliminary root cause: server allowed client-specified `max_tokens` without enforcement; streaming path didn't apply the same preflight checks as non-streaming. Combined with a client that omitted `stop` (or had no sensible termination), it triggered runaway generation and OOMs.
Maya (SRE): Escalation: we'll keep this P1 until postmortem. Action items:
- Runtime: add server-side preflight validation for `max_tokens` and `stop` presence for streaming (Eli) - ETA 48h
- Edge: implement global streaming concurrency soft-limits per API key (Maya) - ETA 24h
- Product: review API defaults and docs to make `max_tokens` cap obvious (Omar) - ETA 72h
- Customer Ops: finalize outbound emails & support tickets (Jane) - in progress
Bob (oncall): Handoff to Maya for longtail remediation. I'm going offline for 1h. Details: affected nodes runtime-decode-21-{7bf4,8a9c,3f11,cc22}, API key acct_7X.. flagged. See logs under `/var/log/runtime/ooms/1793754321/`.
Maya (SRE): Taking over. I'll coordinate the postmortem and run the fix PRs. Drafting a short mitigation runbook update now.
incident_bot: NOTE: paging history recorded. Incident assigned ID: INC-2026-0315-09. Postmortem required.
Omar (Product): For postmortem include: when clamp was applied, why streaming missed validation, recommended SLA credits if customers impacted more than 5% over 15m.
Eli (Runtime): Quick follow-up: we'll add an internal test that simulates streaming sessions with `max_tokens` in [1..10000] and verifies memory bounds. I'll open PR with tests and server-side clamp flag.
Jane (Customer Ops): Email draft posted in #customer-notifs, ping me for sign-off. Early apologies and remediation steps included.
Maya (SRE): Wrapping: incident state -> mitigated; nodes recovered; root cause -> missing server-side max_tokens validation on streaming; impact -> ~23 dropped requests, 3 enterprise customers affected. Next steps tracked in INC-2026-0315-09.
Bob (oncall): Thanks all. If anything regresses ping me. :thumbsup:
Eli (Runtime): Will follow up with PRs and the memory sim test. Closing my active tasks here.
Jane (Customer Ops): I'll update support tickets and send final customer summary after postmortem.
Maya (SRE): Closing incident chat for rotations. Postmortem draft ETA EOD tomorrow.
